players.product: dedicated bare-metal AI infrastructure (GPU clusters) designed, deployed, owned and operated for enterprises; Axe Compute Build build-to-order program

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue was $3.2 million, the first full quarter of compute revenue, up from $35,000 in Q1 (CFO Jeremy Yaukey-Witter). All compute revenue came from the Access model (on-demand GPU capacity across many locations); Build revenue (dedicated GPU clusters Axe designs, deploys, owns and operates for enterprises) had not yet started and begins at go-live.

Q2 2026 net loss $17.2 million, driven by $13.1 million of losses on digital assets (mainly unrealized fair-value changes on its Ether holdings); adjusted EBITDA approximately -$4.9 million, of which about $0.9 million related to the legacy drug discovery service segment. First-half 2026 operating cash flow was a positive $17.4 million, driven by customer prepayments of $60.8 million at June 30; cash $21.9 million (up from $6.9 million at end of Q1); digital assets (mainly Ether) plus the current digital asset receivable approximately $18.8 million. Contract liabilities (customer prepayments) included $33.6 million expected to be recognized within 12 months and $27.1 million long-term. During the quarter Axe made prepayments to third-party compute suppliers to reserve compute for signed customer contracts with terms of up to three years.
quarterly_data.figure: net loss $17.2 million; adjusted EBITDA approximately -$4.9 million; customer prepayments $60.8 million; cash $21.9 million; contract liabilities $33.6 million current and $27.1 million long-term

quarterly_data.signal: Signed book: $317 million of total contract value through the end of Q2, including the $260 million contract announced in April; an incremental $2.9 billion added in the first half of Q3 (about six weeks), comprising the three build contracts announced in July - more than $3.2 billion of TCV year to date through August (CFO). CEO Christopher Miglino: more than $3 billion in signed contracts, all on a take-or-pay basis with multi-year contracts, and more than $500 million in customer prepayments; nearly $3 billion of additional agreements were signed in the quarter versus the roughly $1 billion the company had expected. He announced receipt of the first prepayment of $317 million+ for the cluster being expanded.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $3.2 billion TCV year to date through August; $317 million TCV through Q2; $2.9 billion added in first half of Q3; more than $500 million customer prepayments; first prepayment $317 million+

quarterly_data.signal: Run-rate outlook (CFO): exit annualized run rate leaving Q2 was $37 million; as the April cluster goes live in Q3 it climbs to roughly $139 million (including Access growth to date); once the full signed book is deployed, spanning Q4 into Q1 of next year, the company expects an annualized run rate north of $696 million. CEO: the Columbus, Georgia cluster alone should contribute around $20 million to $21 million a quarter once live, growing to the $696 million ARR as other clusters come on from the end of Q4 into Q1. A contract enters run rate only once deployed and billing.
quarterly_data.figure: exit run rate $37 million; roughly $139 million after April cluster goes live; north of $696 million at full deployment; Columbus cluster $20 million-$21 million a quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Signing target: the company's objective is an additional $2 billion in signed contracts before the end of 2026; CEO Christopher Miglino says he does not think hitting it will be a problem and that, if things keep going as in the last quarter, it should exceed that goal. President Kyle Okamoto: more than 20 people are being added, each hire funded by a signed contract.
quarterly_data.figure: additional $2 billion signed contracts targeted before end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline (President Kyle Okamoto): $5.9 billion of active qualified pipeline across 98 open opportunities as of August, nearly double the signed book; by dollar value roughly 2/3 of that demand is for Blackwell-class GPUs or Vera Rubin (B200, B300, GB200, Vera Rubin), and the company is already fielding significant early demand for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin ahead of volume shipment. Its deployments span 5, 15 and 30-MW AI factories across a U.S. and European footprint.
quarterly_data.figure: $5.9 billion active qualified pipeline; 98 open opportunities; roughly 2/3 Blackwell-class or Vera Rubin

quarterly_data.signal: Build contract structure and modeled economics (CEO Christopher Miglino): customers want dedicated capacity on 5-year to 10-year terms; each project has a customer down payment of 20%-45% of project cost upfront. Management's own model of steady-state build-project economics (blended across signed build contracts, described as forward-looking and not guidance) shows gross margins of 28%-44% and EBITDA margins of 62%-76%.
quarterly_data.figure: customer down payment 20%-45% of project cost; modeled gross margins 28%-44%; modeled EBITDA margins 62%-76%

quarterly_data.signal: Columbus, Georgia NVIDIA B300 cluster (the first build deal, announced in April) is set to go live in the coming weeks; President Kyle Okamoto: the cluster uses an InfiniBand spine-leaf architecture with about 6.4 terabits per second of communication between GPUs and high-speed storage supporting over 20 PB of data, and will be expanded into one contiguous single-spine architecture 3x the size, tripling in the next few months. CEO: much of what is being deployed will go live by the end of the year into the beginning of the first quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: go-live in coming weeks; about 6.4 terabits per second GPU interconnect; over 20 PB storage; expansion to 3x the size

players.product: GB200 / GB300 / Vera Rubin GPU systems

connects_to.relationship: B300 / GB300 NVL72 GPUs and NVIDIA switching for Axe Compute GPU clusters

contracts.signal: Axe Compute President Kyle Okamoto: every Axe cluster starts with NVIDIA silicon - eight B300 GPUs per node with 288 GB of HBM3E on each; the largest builds use the GB300 NVL72 (72 GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs in one rack); the Columbus, Georgia cluster follows an NVIDIA reference design with full NVIDIA switching and full NVIDIA GPUs throughout.
contracts.units: eight B300 GPUs per node; GB300 NVL72 racks for the largest builds

connects_to.relationship: Dell servers for cluster bridges and management functions

contracts.signal: Axe Compute President Kyle Okamoto, touring the Columbus, Georgia B300 cluster: Dell boxes are being used for some of the cluster's bridges and management capabilities.
